extracted.intended_audience: prospective and current USPTO patent and trademark practitioners, and members of the public seeking practitioner information
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for who may practice before the USPTO in patent and trademark matters, plus OED roles (exam administration, discipline, pro bono and clinic programs). Covers eligibility, registration exam, disciplinary oversight, and practitioner-finding resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registered patent practitioner eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Registered patent practitioners are individuals who have passed the USPTO's registration exam and met the qualifications to represent patent applicants before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prospective patent practitioners must apply for registration, satisfy established qualifications, and pass the USPTO registration exam; the Office of Enrollment and Discipline (OED) administers the registration exam and maintains the roster of current patent practitioners. See linked 'Becoming a patent practitioner' resource for requirements, forms, and exam information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark practitioner eligibility (bar standing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Trademark practitioners are attorneys who are active members in good standing of the bar of the highest court of any State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To represent others in trademark matters before the USPTO an attorney must be an active, in-good-standing member of a State's highest court bar. See 'Becoming a trademark practitioner' and 'Finding a trademark practitioner' links for more information and resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: OED administration of registration and practitioner roster
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office of Enrollment and Discipline (OED) administers the registration exam and maintains a roster of current patent practitioners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OED publishes information and updates about the registration exam (e.g., 'Registration exam update'), posts 'Registration to practice' notices and Federal Register / Official Gazette notices, and provides contacts for administrative questions. Practitioners and applicants should consult OED notices for current procedures and requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disciplinary oversight and grievance investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: OED investigates grievances submitted against practitioners and provides public information about disciplinary actions against practitioners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners are subject to investigation and possible discipline; OED will publish information about disciplinary actions and maintains processes for submitting grievances. Individuals and clients can consult OED resources for ethics rules, common forms, and access to disciplinary information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Pro Bono Program coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: OED coordinates a nationwide Patent Pro Bono Program for under-resourced inventors seeking free legal help.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program links eligible inventors with volunteer practitioners; OED coordinates the program but eligibility and referral details are provided via the program resources. Inventors should consult the Patent Pro Bono Program guidance to determine suitability and procedures for obtaining pro bono assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Law School Clinic Certification Program administration
rubrics_metrics.description: OED administers a Law School Clinic Certification Program where law students gain experience in intellectual property law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program certifies law school clinics to represent clients in certain USPTO matters, enabling supervised law students to gain practical IP experience. Law schools and clinics should follow OED certification requirements and procedures described in the program materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resources for finding and maintaining practitioner information
rubrics_metrics.description: The page points to resources for 'Finding a patent practitioner', 'Information for current practitioners', 'Finding a trademark practitioner', and OED Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members of the public can use these resources to locate registered agents/attorneys, and practitioners can access ethics rules, common forms, and online access tools. Administrative notices (Registration to practice, OED Federal Register notices, OED Official Gazette notices) provide transparency about applicants and practitioner status.
